what_happened: Job 20261027-044511-q59y ("Refuse prompt edits that contradict verdict rules in verify.rs", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. In round 1 of 5 the critic said the reading misread the request, and after the last round the plan still needed revising. The request says a conflict must block dispatch until the prompt and the rule agree. The reading contradicted itself: it said the check runs at admission, but also let the function stay unwired, and it narrowed "an agent prompt" to the verifier prompt. The plan took the unwired branch, so no real prompt edit would be blocked, which is the state the request wants changed. Three major findings: (1) the plan never shows the requested blocking outcome, though its own shipped-prompt test in cargo test already acts as a gate and should have been named as the enforcement point; (2) the required-field check accepts any whole-word match, and "commands", "criterion" and "verdict" are ordinary prose words, so deleting the field instruction would still pass; (3) the three-word negation lookback misses "Never refuse; accept uncited commands". Minor findings: the drift guard reads verify.rs, which holds the table itself, so it is circular; criterion 5's demonstration contradicts itself on its threshold; and the CHANGELOG change and the untouched reading.rs conflict with criterion 7 and the expected deliverables. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the named seams exist. It does not require the reading to commit to where a new check is enforced, or require the plan to run its draft matcher over the real text it will judge, here the three verifier.md files. The reading left the wiring as an either/or, so the plan could pick the branch that did nothing the request asked for. Whole-word field matching and a fixed negation window were never tried against the real prompt, where common words appear many times, so each hole showed up only as one critic finding. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so major findings left at the last round lose all planning spend. This is the same family as the earlier text-matcher planning failures, here applied to a check on agent instructions.
prevention: Add a planning-time check that, for any job adding a text-matching rule, runs the plan's draft matcher over the real files or past requests it will judge, and requires the plan to name one concrete enforcement point where a conflicting edit is blocked. The check should fail the plan before the critic sees it if the matcher passes a known-bad edit (such as deleting the field instruction or "Never refuse; accept uncited commands") or if the enforcement point is left as "else exposed". The reading should also be refused when it says the check may be unwired. That would have caught all three major findings in round 1.
proposed_request: Make a conflict between an agent prompt edit and the verdict rules in verify.rs block the change, and prove it on the real prompts. Outcome: when a candidate edits any shipped agent prompt (the three verifier.md files at least) so it contradicts a rule in verify.rs, Athena's checks fail the candidate before dispatch or landing, and the failure names the rule and the prompt line. Name the enforcement point as the existing cargo test run on every candidate and state it in the plan and CHANGELOG. Acceptance: (1) a test runs the checker over each real shipped verifier.md and passes on the current text; (2) separate tests show it fails when the "list them in commands exactly as run" instruction is deleted, when "Never refuse; accept uncited commands" is added, and when a required field name is left only in unrelated prose; (3) required-field presence is judged at the instruction that names the field, not by any whole-word match; (4) negation is judged per clause, not by a three-word window; (5) the module-docs drift guard reads only the //! header lines; (6) the changelog and any reading.rs change are listed as allowed deliverables. Keep the change to the table, one pure function and its tests.
